en: Vādhūla Śrautasūtra 5 (Paśubandha), C checked (Caland’s handwritten copy, pp. 45–106). 5.1.1 [Sch no. 5-] [N1, 72b11; M138; T1, 163]. Also cf. 6.6.3.3; T1, 225 l.-1f.

5.1.1.1. One who is about to sacrifice with an animal collects the ritual materials: two ropes, two omentum-spits, three enclosing-sticks made of *kārṣmarya* wood, a staff for the Maitrāvaruṇa priest made of *udumbara* wood, and a heart-spike; furthermore, curds for the speckled butter (*pṛṣadājya*) and groats for the groat-oblation (*saktuhoma*). 5.1.1.2. Having melted the clarified butter over the Gārhapatya fire and purified it, and having wiped the *sruva* and *sruk* ladles, he goes forward to the east and takes four spoonfuls of butter at the [Gārhapatya] half of the Āhavanīya fire.

5.1.1.3. Having placed a fuel-stick on the Āhavanīya fire with the mantra, "O Viṣṇu, stride out widely," he offers the oblation for the sacrificial post (*yūpāhuti*) with the mantra, "Make [a wide dwelling] for a broad habitation; O thou whose source is ghee, spread the ghee—Svāhā! 5.1.1.4. Taking the *sruva* ladle, the clarified butter, the *upāṃśugrahaṇa* vessel, the sacrificial grass (*barhis*), and the axe, he goes forth.
5.1.1.5. He approaches that half of the sacrificial post which he has chosen, saying, "I have gone to others, not to others; [I go] to the one belonging to Viṣṇu for the sacrifice to the gods."
5.1.1.6. With the words, "May Savitṛ, the god, anoint thee" (VS 1.3.5d, with variation), he anoints it with clarified butter while placing a piece of gold between.
5.1.1.7. With the words, "O herb, protect him" (VS 1.3.5e), he encloses it with a blade of *barhis* grass.
5.1.1.8. With the words, "O axe, do not harm him" (VS 1.3.5f), he strikes it with the axe.

5.1.1.9. He ties up the first chip that falls away and sets it aside. 5.1.1.10. He cuts [the tree] so as not to touch the axle; he causes it to be dragged forward, either toward the east or toward the north.
5.1.1.11. He consecrates it with the mantra: "Do not scratch the sky with your top; do not harm the intermediate space with your middle; be united with the earth" (TS 1.3.5g). [No. 6]

5.1.1.12. With the mantra, “O Lord of the Forest, grow with a hundred branches, svāhā! (TS 1.3.5h1), he throws a piece of gold onto the stump where the tree was felled and offers an oblation. 5.1.1.13. With the mantra, “May we grow with a thousand branches” (TS 1.3.5h2), he touches himself. 5.1.1.14. Having touched water, he sharpens the axe-blade along the grain of the wood with the mantra, “Thee, whom this sharpening axe... and continues with “...has led forth for great good fortune. (TS 1.3.5h3–4)
5.1.1.15. With the mantra, “May wealth with excellent heroes be uncut” (TS 1.3.5.i), he trims the *caṣāla* [of the first trunk].
5.1.1.16. In this very same manner, he trims the *caṣāla* of the subsequent trunk by four finger-breadths.
5.1.1.17. They bring these three things.
5.1.1.18. They fashion the sacrificial post (*yūpa*) with eight corners.

5.1.1.19. If they perform the preliminary offering (*iṣṭi*) beforehand, then, having given to the ancestors on the *anvāhāryapacana* fire, having set out the sacrificial implements, and having carried forward the ritual waters, he offers a cake on eight potsherds to Agni. 5.1.1.20. Once the oblation has been poured out, he recites the *prāṇagraha* formulas and the *pṛśni* verses.
5.1.1.20. When [the sacrifice] is near its conclusion, he recites the *apānagraha* verses and the *pṛśni* verses.
5.1.1.21. For this [offering], the two *vārtraghna* verses are the *ājyabhāga* portions.
5.1.1.22. The two *triṣṭubh* verses, "Agni is the head of the world" (*agnir mūrdhā bhuvaḥ*) and [the second], are the *saṃyājyā* verses for the oblation.

5.1.1.23. Following the continuity [of the fire], he offers the oblation with the *hotṛ* (or *juhvat*). 5.1.1.24. The rite is successfully accomplished; this sacrifice comes to a conclusion. 5.1.1.25. If, however, they do not perform the sacrifice, having given [the food] to the ancestors on the *anvāhāryapacana* fire, they prepare the altar to the east of the *āhavanīya* fire.

5.1.1.26. He prepares the altar so that there is space for the chariot immediately in front of the edge of the altar; at the junction [of the front and side], he digs a hole for the sacrificial post (*yūpa*) as deep as the upper part [of the post].

[cf. no. 40, p. 65] 5.1.1.27. From it, he carries away the *staṃbayajus* grass-bundle; he encloses the altar; he mutters the *karaṇa* formula. [no. 14] 5.1.1.28. He issues the call: "The wooden sword (*sphya*), the water-vessel... and "Bring the *śamyā* wood-block! Come, O Sacrificer and Agnīdh, sit down upon the high altar (*uttaravedi*). [cf. no. 18f., p. 22f.]

5.1.1.29. Having dug up the *cātvāla* site with the wooden sword (*sphya*) while reciting, "Lift up the earth for us" (TS 2.4.8f), he sprinkles it with water from a vessel, saying, "Split this heavenly vault; grant us the heavenly [water]; O Lord, release the leather bag. He then measures it around with a yoke-pin (*śamyā*). [The term *kāla* refers to the spot where something is subsequently established; cf. Caland, *ĀpŚS*, I, 156 = (291):6f. [No. 18]

5.1.1.30. Having placed a wooden pin (śamyā) to the south, pointing eastward, he scrapes along the inside with the wooden sword (sphyá), saying, “Thou art my path to wealth” (TS 1.2.12a1); saying, “Thou art my path to refreshment” (ibid. a2), he places one to the west, pointing northward; saying, “Protect me in my distress” (ibid. a3), he places one to the east, pointing northward; and saying, “Protect me in my agitation” (ibid. a4), he places one to the north, pointing eastward. 5.1.1.31. Saying, “Agni knows thee by the name Nabhas, O Agni Aṅgiras” (TS 1.2.12b,c1), he strikes at the middle of the loose soil (purīṣa) with the wooden sword.
5.1.1.32. With the words, “O thou who art on this earth,” he takes it up.
5.1.1.33. With the words, “Come with life unto the name,” he carries it away.

5.1.1.34. With the words, “With that name of thine which is unassailable and worthy of sacrifice, I place thee,” having carried it to the eastern part of the Āgnīdhra, he sets it down upon the high altar (uttaravedi).

5.1.1.35. With the words, "O Agni Aṅgiras," he strikes down the second [firebrand]. With the words, "He who art on the second earth," he takes it up. With the words, "Come with the name Āyus," he carries it away. With the words, "With that name of yours which is unassailable and worthy of sacrifice, I establish you," having carried it to the Āgnīdhra fire-altar by the same way as before, he places it upon the high altar (uttaravedi).

5.1.1.36. With the verse, “O Agni Aṅgiras,” he throws the third [shovelful]. With the words, “Who thou art on the third earth,” he takes it up. With the words, “Come with life unto the name,” he carries it away. With the words, “With that name of thine which is unassailable and worthy of sacrifice, with that I establish thee,” having carried it to the Āgnīdhra fire-altar by the eastern path, he places it upon the high altar (uttaravedī).
5.1.1.37. He carries the fourth shovelful silently. 5.1.1.38. Having moistened it with water, he mixes it together with the words, “Thou art a lioness; thou art a buffalo-cow.”

5.1.1.39. With the formula, "Spread wide—may the lord of the sacrifice spread wide for thee," he spreads [the altar] with the wooden sword (*sphya*). 5.1.1.40. With the formula, "Thou art firm, thou art firm," he strikes it three times with the yoke-pin (*śamyā*).
5.1.1.41. Having made it one span (*prādeśa*) on all sides, well-formed, and four-cornered, he sprinkles it with water with the formula, "Be purified for the gods."
5.1.1.42. With the words, “Be purified for the gods,” they proceed, having made the northern navel [of the altar] non-naked above by means of water and sand.
5.1.1.43. Having covered it with a winnowing basket or with grass, they kindle the sacrificial fuel.
5.1.1.44. They prepare the supporting ladles (upayamanī) and the materials for the high altar (uttaravedi). ||1||

5.1.2.1. The materials for the *uttaravedi* are: bdellium (*gulgulu*), fragrant reed-grass (*sugandhitejana*), a tuft of white wool, enclosing-sticks made of *pautudrava* wood, the drawing of the *upāṃśu* cup, sprinkling waters (*prokṣaṇyaḥ*), and clarified butter taken five times.
5.1.2.2. When the fuel-wood is kindled, he takes four portions [of clarified butter]. 5.1.2.3. He offers that.
5.1.2.4. Having mentally recited the *ṣaḍḍhotṛ* formula, he takes another fourfold portion.

5.1.2.5. He offers that with the verse, "Agni has looked along the forefront of the dawns" (TS 4.1.2.k), and with the word "along" (*anu*) as the point of reference, he says, "The first one has stretched across the days, svāhā! (TS 4.1.2.k; cf. Caland, *Śrautasūtra des Āpastamba*, I, p. 157 = 292). 5.1.2.6. Having offered, he takes a fivefold portion.
5.1.2.7. While lifting the fuel-sticks (*idhma*), they bring forward the supporting ladles (*upayamanī*). 5.1.2.8.
He says, "Recite for the fire as it is being carried forth," and "Run forth with the single wooden sword (*ekasphya*). 5.1.2.9.
Scratching with the wooden sword, he runs forth with the single wooden sword as far as the northern altar (*uttaravedi*).
5.1.2.10. With the words, "The sage extends the path of the sacrifice" (TS 3.5.5f), the Adhvaryu causes the sacrificer to recite.

5.1.2.11. Having stepped over [the altar] with the verse: "Upon the back of the navel, in the luminous realm of heaven, by which thou carriest the oblation as a messenger from here, wise and most bountiful," he sprinkles the northern navel with the formula: "May Indraghoṣa protect thee in the east with the Vasus; may Manojava protect thee in the south with the Pitṛs; may Pracetas protect thee in the west with the Rudras; may Viśvakarman protect thee in the north with the Ādityas; may Bṛhaspati protect thee from above with all the gods. [The portion "Bṛhaspati... protect thee" is not found in the TS.]

5.1.2.12. Whatever remains of the *prokṣaṇī* waters, he pours it out to the south of the *uttaravedi* along the track of the wooden sword (*sphya*). 5.1.2.13. The sacrificer meditates upon whomsoever he hates. 5.1.2.14. Having touched water and taken five portions of clarified butter, having placed a piece of gold [upon the ladle], he sprinkles it crosswise over the northern navel:
5.1.2.15. "Thou art a lioness, overcoming rivals, *svāhā*!"—thus on the southern shoulder.

5.1.2.16. "Thou art a lioness, winning good offspring; svāhā!"—thus on the northern hip. 5.1.2.17. "Thou art a lioness, winning increase of wealth; svāhā!"—thus on the southern hip. 5.1.2.18. "Thou art a lioness, winning the Ādityas; svāhā!"—thus on the northern shoulder.
5.1.2.19. With the formula, “Thou art a lioness; bring hither the gods for the god-loving sacrificer, svāhā!”—thus he offers in the middle.

5.1.2.20. With the formula, “For the beings, thee! he lifts up the offering-spoon (sruk). 5.1.2.21. With the formula, “Thou art all-enlivening; make firm the earth! he lays down the middle enclosing-stick (paridhi) made of *pūtudru* wood.

5.1.2.22. With the formula, "Thou art the stable-seated; make firm the intermediate space," he [places] the southern half. 5.1.2.23. With the formula, "Thou art the immovable-seated; make firm the sky," he [places] the northern half.
5.1.2.24. With the formula, "Thou art the ash of Agni; thou art the soil of Agni," he pours down the ritual materials (*saṃbhārān*).

5.1.2.25. He makes an offering over them with the residue of the ghee, [reciting]: "The gods found that which was hidden in the cave—the domestic animals, multiform, though being of various forms, yet of one form in many ways; may there be delight for those seven in me here, svāhā!
(TA 3.11.12). 5.1.2.26. He pours down the supporting earth. 5.1.2.27. He settles the fire.

5.1.2.28. With the words, “Thou art Prajāpati, the All-maker,” he pays homage to the one who has been laid down, saying, “May that [be] yonder sun, may this [be] fire; may it be well-beloved by the cattle.”

5.1.2.29. He offers the *atimukti* oblations with the formulas: "May Agni, knowing [the way], lead the sacrifice; may those who destroy the sacrifice not find it; announce the sacrifice to the gods; further and further extend the lord of the sacrifice, *svāhā*. May Vāyu, knowing [the way], lead the sacrifice; may those who destroy the sacrifice not find it... extend the lord of the sacrifice, *svāhā*. May Sūrya, knowing [the way], lead the sacrifice; may those who destroy the sacrifice not find it... extend the lord of the sacrifice, *svāhā*. May the Sacrifice itself, knowing [the way], lead the sacrifice; may those who destroy the sacrifice not find it; extend the lord of the sacrifice, *svāhā*. 5.1.2.30. Taking up the wooden sword (*sphya*) and rising, he says: "O Brahman, I shall perform the second tracing of the altar."
5.1.2.31. To the south of the *uttaravedi*, the Brahman sits down.
5.1.2.32. Once permitted, he performs the second tracing out (*parigrāha*).

5.1.2.33. Having leveled [the ground] and propped it up, he issues the call: "Set down the sprinkling waters; place the fuel and the sacrificial grass (*idhmābarhis*) nearby; cleanse the dipping-spoon (*sruva*) and the offering-ladle (*sruk*); gird the wife; come forth with the clarified butter (*ājya*); bring curds for the speckled butter (*pṛṣadājya*); come, O sacrificer!"
5.1.2.34. They perform this [rite].

5.1.2.35. Having wiped the offering-spoons (*srucaḥ*), he takes portions of clarified butter (*ājyāni*) together with the speckled butter (*pṛṣadājya*). 5.1.2.36. Having taken the portions for the *juhū* and *upabhṛt* spoons in the established manner, he makes an under-layer (*upastṛṇīte*) for the speckled butter with the formula: "Thou art the milk of the great ones" (TS 3.2.6a).

5.1.2.37. The second [offering] is with the mantra: "The body of the Viśve Devas. 5.1.2.38. With the mantra: "May I succeed today in the drawing of the speckled ones," he pours curds into the ladle across the filter, saying: "Thou art the draught of the speckled ones. 5.1.2.39.
He pours clarified butter over it from above with the mantra: "Thou art the heart of Viṣṇu, one for food. [Note: The application of the mantras differs from BŚS 4.3:112.15–16.]
5.1.2.40. With the words, “Viṣṇu has stepped across you,” he makes [the sacrificer] recite the second [verse].
5.1.2.41. With the words, “May prosperity increase through curds and ghee,” he causes [the sacrificer] to recite.
5.1.2.42. At the time for the *dhruvā* [ladle], with the words, “Of that which is sacrificed, I take the invincible portion,” he lifts up the vessel of clarified butter.
5.1.2.43. He sprinkles the fuel and the sacrificial grass. || 2 ||

5.1.3 Sūtra No. 38: [K1,33a1–; M143; C65–; T1,169] 5.1.3.1. He sprinkles the fuel-sticks (*idhma*) and the sacrificial grass (*barhis*). He sprinkles the altar (*vedi*). He sprinkles the materials that have been set down.
5.1.3.2. Having poured out the remaining water, he takes up the *prastara* bundle.
5.1.3.3. He strews the sacrificial grass (*barhis*). Having stepped forward toward the east and grasped the sacrificial grass, he lays down the enclosing sticks (*paridhi*).
5.1.3.4. He places two fuel sticks (*samidh*) made of *kārṣmarya* wood. [No. 38a]
5.1.3.5. Having caused [the sacrificer] to recite over the enclosing-sticks (*paridhi*), he yokes the fire.

5.1.3.6. Having returned, he places [the ladles] crosswise: the *tiraścī* [ladle] on the *tiraścī* [stick], the *prastara* [bunch of grass] on the *tiraścī* sticks, the *juhū* on the *prastara*, and the other two [ladles, *upabhṛt* and *dhruvā*] on the sacrificial grass (*barhis*).

5.1.3.7. Having set them down and touched them together with the formula, "The steadfast ones have sat down... that which is mine, O Agni... (cf. MS 1.1.12:8.3; KS 1.11:6; VS 2.6), he recites the *daśahotṛ* formula.

5.1.3.8. Having touched water, he takes up the spade with the formula: "At the impulse of the god Savitṛ... (TS 1.3.1a,b). "With the arms of the Aśvins, with the hands of Pūṣan, I take thee; thou art a spade, thou art a woman. 5.1.3.9. He traces around the hole for the sacrificial post with the formula: "The *rakṣas* is traced out; the enemies are traced out" (TS 1.3.1c). "Here I cut off the neck of the *rakṣas*, whoever... I cut him off. (TS 1.3.1c) [K3,71b5] "I cut him off."
5.1.3.10. He says, "O Pratiprasthātṛ, come here with this sacrificial post, which is measured by the *khara* and the *uparasa*.
5.1.3.11. The post has been fashioned with eight corners, fitted with the *caṣāla* top-ring, and washed; it is then placed to the east of the sacrificial pit (*yūpāvaṭa*). 5.1.3.12.

Walking around it together with two splinters (*śakala*), he issues the command: "Bring the sprinkling waters containing barley, the sacrificial grass (*barhis*), the clarified butter (*ājya*), and the *upāṃśu* cup; come, O sacrificer!"

5.1.3.13. He sprinkles the sacrificial post (*yūpa*) with the formula, “For the earth thee, for the intermediate space thee, for the sky thee” (cf. 1.3.1), and [he adds], “May the world, the seat of the ancestors, be purified. [No. 41] 5.1.3.14.

He pours water into the sacrificial post-hole (*yūpāvaṭa*) with the formula, “Thou art barley; bar away from us our enemies” (1.3.1). 5.1.3.15. He scatters barley-grains [into the hole] with the formula, “Bar away the adversaries” (1.3.1). [K3, 71b7]

5.1.3.16. With the formula, “Thou art the seat of the fathers; svāhā to the fathers,” he spreads out sacrificial grass with its tips pointing in various directions, saying, “svāhā to the fathers. 5.1.3.17. Having placed gold underneath, he makes an oblation of clarified butter while reciting, “Thou art easy of access, O Agregā” (VS 1.3.6e). Then, having said, “The lord of the forest shall stand upon thee; may he know thee,” he places a chip of wood from the sacrificial post with its broad side facing upward. 5.1.3.18. He says, “Recite for the sacrificial post as it is being anointed” (cf. Śatapatha Brāhmaṇa 3.7.1.10; Āpastamba Śrauta Sūtra 7.10.1; Mānava Śrauta Sūtra 1.2.2.12).

5.1.3.19. Reciting, "May the god Savitṛ anoint you with honey" (cf. 1.3.5d; 1.3.6f), having pulled out the *caṣāla* and placed a piece of gold in between, he anoints its tip. 5.1.3.20. Having anointed the *caṣāla* in this very same manner, he fastens it on with the formula, "For the plants that bear good fruit" (1.3.6g).
5.1.3.21. In this very same manner, he anoints the edge facing the fire (*agniṣṭhā*).
5.1.3.22. He touches it three times at the height of the navel. 5.1.3.23. He anoints it up to the end. 5.1.3.24. "Recite for the post as it is being raised," he says.
5.1.3.25. With the words, “Support the sky above (1.3.6h),” he raises [the post], and with, “Fill the intermediate space; make firm the earth below. [No. 43] 5.1.3.26.

With the words, “Tread upon those who attack (B2.4.2.9),” he sets it down, and with, “May the enemies be beneath you; like Indra, the slayer of Vṛtra, stand firm on your side, conquering the treasures. 5.1.3.27.

With two verses addressed to Viṣṇu, beginning with, “We desire to go to those abodes of yours (1.3.6i, k),” he prepares [the site], and with, “Where the cows with many horns are, there our worthy friend is yoked.”

5.1.3.28. When they join the corner facing the fire (agniṣṭhā-aśri) with the Āhavanīya fire, he then causes the top-ring (caṣāla) to be raised up with the verse, “That highest step of Viṣṇu” (RV 1.22.20), and with the words, “They always behold it spread out.

5.1.3.29. With the formula, “The winner of the Brahman, the winner of the Kṣatra” (RV 1.22.21), he piles earth around it, saying, “I pile thee around as the winner of good progeny and the winner of the increase of wealth.”

5.1.3.30. "O Brahman, make firm; O Kṣatra, make firm"—with these words, he makes it firm with the staff of the Maitrāvaruṇa, [saying]: "Make the offspring firm, make wealth firm, make the increase of riches firm, make the kinsmen firm for the sacrificer.
5.1.3.31. With the verse, "Make the earth swell" (TS 2.4.8f), he pours out a vessel of water [saying]: "Break this divine skin. 5.1.3.32.
One should not release the sacrificial post before the time of the encircling.
5.1.3.32. He says, "Recite for her as she is being girt about.
5.1.3.33. With the formula, "Thou art girt about" (TS 1.3.6.o), he girds it around her at the level of the navel with the formula, "The divine [girdle] has girt thee, O human one.
5.1.3.34. Having girt it three times, he causes the end to enter [inside].
5.1.3.35. He spreads out the *aṇiman* and *sthavimat* [woolen strainers].
5.1.3.36. With the mantra, “Thou art the son of heaven” (*divaḥ sūnur asi*), he takes up the tone.
5.1.3.37. With the mantra, “I conceal thee on the ridge of the intermediate space” (*antarikṣasya tvā sānāv avagūhāmi*), he conceals it within the middle enclosing-stalk (*parivyaya*).
5.1.3.38. He releases the sacrificial post (yūpa) at the end of the *sakala* [formula]. || 3 ||
Thus ends the first section.

5.2.1 [The Dedication of the Animal Sacrificial Victim, Schwab no. 45] [K1,33a10–; C66; M145; T1,171] 5.2.1.1. With the formula, “For food, thee” (TS 1.3.7a), he takes two blades of sacrificial grass (*barhis*).

5.2.1.2. With the formulas, “Born of Prajāpati... (TS 3.1.4a, b; both with *svāhā*), he offers the two oblations of dedication: “May Prajāpati... (TS 3.1.4a)... approve, *svāhā*; this offering... (TS 3.1.4b)... *svāhā*.”

5.2.1.3. With the formula, “Thou art the invoker (upavīr asi),” he dedicates the animal facing westward from the east, saying, “Come hither to the gods... [1.3.7b–g] ...rejoice; I dedicate thee, acceptable to Indra and Agni. 5.2.1.4. Having set aside two recognized blades of sacrificial grass (*barhis*), he takes a chip of wood with the formula, “Thou art the birthplace of Agni,” and [another chip with] “Ye two are the testicles; be born after the Jāgata metre. 5.2.1.5.
He says, “Recite for Agni while being churned.”
5.2.1.6. They churn the fire. 5.2.1.7. He says: "Recite for the one born; recite for the one being thrown. 5.2.1.8.
With the words, "Be of one mind with us (1.3.7n,o)," he throws [the firebrand], [saying] "May you two be our peaceful dwellings... today for us."

5.2.1.9. Having offered [the wood] with the words, “Fire moves, having entered into fire, svāhā,” he makes an additional offering over it with the words, “The portion of the Ṛṣis, svāhā. 5.2.1.10. Having touched water, he takes up the rope with his hand turned upward, saying, “At the impulse of the god Savitṛ...; I take you with the arms of the Aśvins and the hands of Pūṣan. [Note: The mantra in 1.3.8a is simply “I take”; is this a condensed form of the mantra? [Schroeder no. 48, p. 81f.]

5.2.1.11. With the formula, “Thee, the oblation for the gods, I seize with the noose of Ṛta” (TS 1.3.8b), he passes [the cord] around the horn of the animal crosswise. 5.2.1.12. With the formula, “Be bold against men” (TS 1.3.8c), he yokes [it].
5.2.1.13. They bring for him the sprinkling waters in a vessel... with the formula, “I sprinkle thee for the waters and the plants; acceptable to Indra and Agni” (TS 1.3.8d).

5.2.1.14. With the words, “Thou art the drinker of waters” (TS 1.3.8e,f), he makes [the horse] drink, [reciting: “Even though already consumed by fire, do not let him die” (TS 1.3.8f). 5.2.1.15. If it should not drink, or if it should not even die, one should whisper into its right ear: “Thou art not slain; living, thou goest by the paths leading to heaven. May he pierce with what is born and with what is yet to be born. Do not abandon this oblation which we approach. It certainly drinks then. 5.2.1.16. Having sprinkled the chest, he sprinkles the back.
5.2.1.17. Having caused [the sacrificer] to drink, having sprinkled [water], and having set down the vessel, he recites the invitatory verse for the fire being kindled.

5.2.1.18. When the *sāmidhenī* verses have been recited, having poured the *āghāra* libation with the *sruva* spoon, he says: "O *Āgnīdh*, cleanse the fire three times each [with the *paridhis*]. 5.2.1.19. Without letting the two *sruks* touch each other, having stepped across [the altar], he anoints the animal with the *juhū* ladle while reciting: "(May your breath go toward the light... [1.3.8g]; and with the words, "May it be well through the worshipful ones... [1.3.9g], ending with the word "blessing" (*āśis*).
5.2.1.20. Having anointed the *dhruvā* ladle and set it down, he should choose the *pravara*.
5.2.1.21. He causes the announcement to be made; he says, "Make the announcement! 5.2.1.22. With the words, "Agni, the god, O gods, is the protector," he chooses Dhātṛ as his *pravara*.
5.2.1.23. He says to him, “What is your name? He announces his name, saying, “I am so-and-so, a human being.
5.2.1.24. In the Āhavanīya fire... the name of the Hotṛ is [inserted]. 5.2.1.25. From this point on, he causes the announcement to be made; he says, “Make the announcement! (āśrāvaya).

5.2.1.26. “Agni is the leader of the divine clans; this sacrificer is the leader of men. May their household fire shine undivided for a hundred winters. O Vāyu, may you two, bestowing gifts upon one another, yet not competing with each other, protect our bodies. 5.2.1.27. At this time, he hands the staff to the Maitrāvaruṇa priest. || 4 ||
At this time, he hands the staff to the Maitrāvaruṇa. 5.2.2.2.
With the words, “The cows chose you for kingship” (TS 3.3.9e), he causes the sacrificer to recite over the Maitrāvaruṇa’s staff: “They call upon you... [for wealth]” (TS 3.3.9e).

5.2.2.3. The Hotṛ sits down. Being impelled, he takes up the two offering-spoons and performs the *prayāja* offerings. He says, "Call for the *āśrāvaṇa*," and then, "Prompt [the Āgnīdhra] for the *samidhs*. 5.2.2.4. He performs eleven *prayāja* offerings.
5.2.2.5. Having poured half [of the butter] into [the *ājyasthālī*] at the fourth [offering], he pours the whole [remaining butter] in at the eighth.
5.2.2.6. Having offered ten oblations from the *upabhṛt* ladle while leaving the eleventh remaining, he steps across.

5.2.2.7. Taking hold of both the *svaru* chip and the sharp-edged axe (*svadhiti*), he anoints the *svaru* on the inner side of the ladle with the formula, “Anointed with ghee,” and the axe on the outer side.
5.2.2.8. With the formula, “May you two protect the animal,” he rubs the axe against the forehead of the animal. He says, “May this edge of yours be sharpened.”

5.2.2.9. While handing over the knife to the slaughterer with which he touches the animal, and having concealed the *svaru* and set down the two offering-ladles in their proper places, he says, "Recite for the fire carried around. [No. 63, p. 96]

5.2.2.10. Having taken a firebrand from the *āhavanīya* fire and gone out between the *cātvāla* and the *utkara*, he performs the circumambulation three times by moving forward with the firebrand, saying: "May they know; may they take hold" (*prajānantu parīgṛhnantu*; cf. TS *prajānantaḥ pratigṛhṇanti*), with the word *svāhā* added to each mantra (as in 3.1.4c–g). While holding the firebrand in his hand, he runs around [the altar]. He offers the five *apāvya* formulas: "The breath... 3.1.4.c ... [with] bodies, *svāhā*; those of whom [he] is the lord... l.c. d ... [and so on].

"May they be [well-disposed], svāhā! Those who [are aware of] the one being bound... svāhā! Those who are wild... svāhā! Those who are aware... svāhā! Releasing... svāhā!"—thus he says. (Sch No. 64) 5.2.2.11. Having said "O sacrificer," while the sacrificer has taken hold [of him], the Hotṛ offers the sixth oblation. 5.2.2.12. Having set down the firebrand, the Āgnīdhra runs back three times along the same path. (No. 65)

5.2.2.13. The Āgnīdhra takes up that very firebrand (ulmuka), the Adhvaryu two blades of sacrificial grass (barhis), and the Pratiprasthātṛ the two omentum-spits (vapāśrapaṇī). They go toward the north, with the firebrand leading. 5.2.2.14. Between the Cātvāla pit and the Utkara mound, having called for the formal announcement (āśrāvya) and given the direction (upapreṣya), he says: "O Hotṛ, [announce] the oblations to the gods. 5.2.2.15.

With the formula, "O wealthy ones, enter the lord of the sacrifice with what is dear" (TS 1.3.8.i=k), they touch the animal with the two omentum-spits, saying, "O wide mid-space, place [the animal]... (TS 1.3.8.k).

5.2.2.16. With the words, “Protect [the animal] from contact with the earth” (TS 1.3.8.l), they strew sacrificial grass (*barhis*) and place the animal upon it, with its head toward the west and its feet toward the north, making it free from groaning.
5.2.2.17. He says, “Slay it gently,” and [later], “Announce that it has been slain.

5.2.2.18. Therefore, according to the text, “The breath of the sacrificer is not separate from the animal” (TS 3.1.4.h), both the Adhvaryu and the sacrificer withdraw from one another, [thinking], “The sacrifice... [is] desires” (TS 3.1.4).
5.2.2.19. Having arrived, they look at the speckled butter (pṛṣadājya), saying: "May offspring rejoice here! [5] 5.2.3.

"May offspring of every form delight here; may those who know all things, dwelling together with Agni, their home, as the ghee-dripping ones, protect us with milk and ghee. [cf. B3.7.4j, which partially agrees]

5.2.3.2. Restraining their speech and not looking around, they sit. 5.2.3.3. When the animal has been quieted, he offers a spoonful with the formula: “Whatever lowing the animal has made, svāhā!”—and when it has been slaughtered, he offers a spoonful with the formula: “The breast of the victim, from distress, svāhā! 5.2.3.4. With the formula, “O slaughterers, come hither,” they approach the animal with the two omentum-spits, [reciting]: “Around the sacrifice... [as in the cited passage].

5.2.3.5. ... [he places] the noose upon the necks... [and then] he loosens them with the formula, "May Aditi loosen this noose" (TS 3.1.4), and he fastens it with "Homage... [to the noose]" (TS 3.1.4). 5.2.3.6. He ties it to a dry stump. The sacrificer meditates upon whomever he hates. 5.2.3.7.
Having sprinkled water around [the fire], they return without looking back.
5.2.3.8. The Pratiprasthātṛ leads the wife away together with the water for washing the feet (*pānnejana*), between the *cātvāla* pit and the *utkara* heap.
5.2.3.9. With the formula, "Unassailable, go forward" (TS 1.3.8n), he leads her toward the north; with the formula, "Of ghee... with the abundance of wealth" (TS 1.3.8).

5.2.3.10. Having returned, he causes the vital breaths of the animal to swell with water by sprinkling it while reciting: "May your speech swell" for the speech; "may your breath swell" for the breath; "may your eye swell" for the eye; and "may your ear swell" for the ear. [Sch No. 75]

5.2.3.11. With the words, “That which has entered into your breaths, that which [has entered] your eye, that which [has entered] your ear... let [it] be purified,” he touches the navel with the words, “May your navel swell”; the anus with the words, “May your anus swell”; and the penis with the words, “May your penis swell. 5.2.3.12. Having placed his feet together with the words, “Pure are your ways,” he sprinkles water. He says, “Peace to the waters, peace to the plants,” and “Peace to the earth, peace to the days.”

5.2.3.13. With the verse, “O divine waters, you who seek purity” (1.3.8), he consecrates the water that has been poured out, saying: “Purified, may you... [1.3.8... ...may we become. [cf. p. 109] 5.2.3.14. The wife returns, and [the Adhvaryu] says: “Make it slightly turned upward, like an animal. [“Kavā”: see Cal Ī, 155:8. Vy: “Slightly turned upward, so that the dissection may proceed by turning on the right side; thus, O immolators, place it.”]
5.2.3.15. With the formula, "O herb, protect him," he covers the skin over the navel with the *barhis* grass on the right side.
5.2.3.16. With the formula, "O axe, do not harm him," he cuts across [the skin] with the axe.
5.2.3.17. Having cut off a thick portion of the *barhis*, he anoints it on both sides of the animal.
5.2.3.18. He throws it away with the formula: “Thou art the portion of the Rakṣases; this I lead away... (1.3.9i,k). 5.2.3.19.
Having touched water, he extracts the omentum with the formula: “For strength thee” (1.3.9l). 5.2.3.20. With ghee, [he anoints] heaven and earth. 5. [6?]

T1,176] 5.2.4.1. With the formula, “O Heaven and Earth, cover yourselves with clarified butter” (TS 1.3.9m), he covers the two omentum-spits. 5.2.4.2. He undercuts them with a blade of *aviśāla* grass.
5.2.4.3. He encloses [the vessel] with the mantra: "May wealth come to us, accompanied by brave sons" (TS 1.3.9n).
5.2.4.4. With the mantra: "Be purified for the gods; be purified for the gods," he wipes the trimming-waste of the sacrificial grass (*barhis*) with the grass itself.
5.2.4.5. Having sprinkled [the vessel] with water from a water-pot, he heats it over a firebrand with the mantra: "The demon is burnt away; the enemies are burnt away."

5.2.4.6. Having drawn out the embers from the *śāmitra* fire with the formula, “Follow the wide mid-region” (TS 1.3.9.o), they return again, led by the firebrand, between the *cātvāla* pit and the rubbish heap (*utkara*).

5.2.4.7. They take hold of the omentum-spits again. With the three *gāyatrī* verses beginning, “Towards thee, O Agni, day by day” (TS 1.5.6.f–i), they approach the *āhavanīya* fire with the verse, “O illuminator of the darkness... for our well-being” (TS 1.5.6.f, g, i). 5.2.4.8. With the formula, “The demon is burnt away; the enemies are burnt away,” he heats [the implements] on the last ember of the *āhavanīya* fire.
5.2.4.9. Having carried it between the sacrificial post (*yūpa*) and the *āhavanīya* fire, the *pratiprasthātṛ*, turning toward the north from the south, roasts the omentum (*vapā*).

5.2.4.10. For that [omentum], the *adhvaryu* throws a blade of grass outside [the fire] with the formula, “O Vāyu, partake of the drops! He makes an oblation upon it with the dipping-spoon (*sruva*) while reciting, “Thee they have established as the bearer of oblations,” and [concludes] with, “When it is cooked, ... enjoy it, svāhā! [cf. ŚB 3.1.4]

5.2.4.11. He says, “Recite for the drops (*stoka*). When the Maitrāvaruṇa has recited this hymn together with its verses, the Adhvaryu, taking up the *praisha* for the *svāhākṛti* offerings, steps across [the altar].

5.2.4.12. He says, “Call for the *āśrāvaṇa*. He issues the command for the *svāhākṛti* offerings. At the utterance of *vaṣaṭ*, he makes the offering. 5.2.4.13. Having sprinkled the speckled butter (*pṛṣadājya*) over it, he sprinkles it over the omentum (*vapā*).
5.2.4.14. He spreads clarified butter and a chip of gold beneath the omentum.
5.2.4.15. He says: "Recite for Indra and Agni as the omentum and fat of the goat are being cut off.
5.2.4.16. Having cut the omentum with the dipping-spoon (sruva), he bastes it from above with both the chip of gold and the clarified butter.
5.2.4.17. Having brought [the items] back by the same way they had come, the Pratiprasthātṛ stands to the north holding the two omentum-spits (vapāśrapaṇī).

5.2.4.18. He says, "Call for the Śrauṣaṭ! [The Āgnīdhra responds, "Oṁ śrauṣaṭ," and the Adhvaryu says: "Prompt [the Hotṛ] regarding the fat and the omentum of the goat set forth for Indra and Agni; [utter] 'Svāhā to the gods! 5.2.4.19. To the east of the omentum, the Pratiprasthātṛ offers a spoonful (sruvāhuti) with the mantra: "O Jātavedas, go to the gods with the omentum, Svāhā! At the utterance of the Vaṣaṭ-call, he offers [another oblation] with: "For you indeed... [3.1.4ṇ] ...the gods, Svāhā!"

5.2.4.20. With the formula, “Svāhā to the gods! (cf. 3.1.40), he makes an additional offering from above with the dipping-spoon (*sruva*), saying, “Svāhā! Go to the Maruts of the upward sky. 5.2.4.21. He throws away the two omentum-spits (*vapāśrapaṇī*) in opposite directions: the wide one toward the east and the narrow one toward the west. He sprinkles them with the drippings of the omentum. 5.2.4.22. Having performed the rite with the omentum, they purify themselves at the *cātvāla* pit with the three verses beginning, “O Waters, you are indeed the source of bliss” (*apo hi ṣṭhā mayobhuva*). 6. [7?]
Thus ends the second section.
5.3.1 [M150; T1,177] 5.3.1.1. The Agnīdh offers the sacrificial cake for the animal victim (paśupuroḍāśa).
5.3.1.2. He issues the command: "O Brahman, guard the speckled butter; O Pratiprasthātṛ, dissect the animal!"

5.3.1.3. They do this: the *agnīdh* offers the animal-cake (*paśupuroḍāśa*) for Indra and Agni on eleven potsherds. The *brahmā* guards the speckled butter (*pṛṣadājya*). The *pratiprasthātṛ* dissects the animal: the heart, the tongue, and the breast—these three; the fat and the kidneys... the left hip. 5.3.1.4. "The rectum, the upper part, and these three limbs: the left foreleg with one bone, the two sides to be placed in the vessel, the right hip, the upper part of the spine, the omentum, and the large intestine (*vaniṣṭhu*). Whatever fat there is, place that in the vessel. Of the three times moved [from the body], make the heart the last," he says.
5.3.1.5. The Āgnīdhra, having removed the animal cake (*paśupuroḍāśa*) after spreading a base of clarified butter and pouring a libation over it, places it within the altar (*antarvedi*).

5.3.1.6. Then he says, while spreading the base of butter: "Recite for the cake as it is being cut off for Indra and Agni. 5.3.1.7. He cuts portions from both the rear and the front into the *juhū* ladle; he pours a libation over them and anoints the blade [of the knife].
5.3.1.8. He cuts [the portion] once from the northern [part] into the *upabhṛt* [ladle]. He pours clarified butter over it twice. He does not anoint it back. 5.3.1.9.
Having joined [the ladles], the Adhvaryu places them [on the fire]. 5.3.1.10.
He says, “Call for the *śrauṣaṭ*!”—he gives the command regarding the cake set forth for Indra and Agni. At the utterance of *vaṣaṭ*, he makes the offering.
5.3.1.11. He says, "Recite the invitatory verse for Agni.

5.3.1.12. While bringing together the *sviṣṭakṛt* portion of the sacrificial cake (*puroḍāśa*), he says, "O Āśrāvya, cause [the announcement]! and then, "Prompt [the Hotṛ] for Agni! 5.3.1.13. When the *vaṣaṭ* has been uttered, he makes the offering.

5.3.1.14. Having stepped across and set down the two offering-spoons (*srucau*) in their respective places, and having divided the portions (*avadānāni*) and sprinkled them with clarified butter, he places the *iḍā* portion before the Hotṛ.
5.3.1.15. When the *iḍā* has been invoked, he places it before the Āgnīdhra.

5.3.1.16. They consume [the portions] and perform the purification (*mārjana*). Together with the vessel, he carries the sacrificial cake (*puroḍāśa*) around to the north of the Āhavanīya fire, together with water, for the Brahman priest.
5.3.1.17. The Brahman eats [the sacrificial food] and performs the ritual purification (mārjana).

5.3.1.18. The Āgnīdhra issues the command: "O Pratiprasthātṛ, perform the formal consultation regarding the animal sacrifice with the words, 'O Adhvaryu, come hither to the northern sacrificial grass'.
5.3.1.19. They perform this [rite].
5.3.1.20. The *agnīdh* fetches a branch of a *plakṣa* tree and places it upon the basket of leaves.

5.3.1.21. With the formula, "For the protection of the gods," the *pratiprasthātṛ* scoops up some speckled butter (*pṛṣadājya*) with the dipping-spoon (*sruva*), saying, "The most brilliant of the brilliant ones.

5.3.1.22. Stepping aside and approaching with the offering-ladle (*sruk*), he asks, "Is the oblation cooked, O *śamitṛ*? He replies, "It is cooked. [The priest says: "May Pūṣan protect that for the gods from the path."

5.3.1.23. Stepping aside, he asks: "Is the oblation cooked, O Śamitṛ? "It is cooked," he replies. "May Pūṣan, the protector of cattle, protect that for the gods. 5.3.1.24. Stepping aside, he asks: "Is the oblation cooked, O Śamitṛ? "It is cooked," he replies. "May Pūṣan, the overlord of the gods, protect that. 5.3.1.25. Before the sprinkling [of clarified butter], he causes the heart to touch the heart-spike.
5.3.1.25. He places it down in its known position. 5.3.1.26.

Having made the heart the uppermost part, he sprinkles it with speckled butter (pṛṣadājya) while reciting: "May your mind be at peace with the mind; may the breath, being dear to the gods, be at peace through the breath; [may this be] ghee-filled, svāhā! 5.3.1.27.
Having carried it between the sacrificial post (yūpa) and the Āhavanīya fire, he sets it down to the south.

5.3.1.28. While spreading [the underlayer] over the four [portions], the Pratiprasthātṛ says: “Recite for the Manotā as the oblation is being cut off. 5.3.1.29. From the *juhū*, the *upabhṛt*, the *vasāhomīyā* vessel, and the *iḍāpātra*, he cuts portions twice from the heart into the *juhū*. He cuts twice from the tongue, twice from the breast, twice from the flank, and twice from each of the two kidneys. 5.3.1.30. Having separated the three parts [of the rectum], he divides the *guda* (rectal portion) into three. Having split the middle section into two, he places it into the *juhū*.

5.3.1.31. He places the largest pieces from the apaya portions. 5.3.1.32. Having placed two small pieces for the Sviṣṭakṛt offering, he cuts portions from the left foreleg; twice from each of the two sides; and twice from the right hip, from the shoulder-blade, and from the last rib. He sprinkles it with broth. 5.3.1.33.
Having poured broth over it, he covers it with fat, pours clarified butter over it, and anoints it back [with the fat].
5.3.1.34. He cuts off a large piece of loose flesh from the right foreleg of the animal.
5.3.1.35. He places that into the *upabhṛt* ladle; he also places a small piece of the rectum into the *upabhṛt* itself. 5.3.1.36.
He cuts off a large piece of flesh from the left buttock.

5.3.1.37. He places that very [piece] into the *upabhṛt* ladle. He pours broth over it. 5.3.1.38. Having placed the broth, he covers it with fat. He pours [clarified butter] over it twice. He does not anoint it back. 5.3.1.39.
Having let the fat-offering (*vasāhoma*) drip from the animal, he pours [clarified butter] over it.
5.3.1.40. He scatters the boneless parts into the *iḍā*-vessel and sprinkles them with broth. 5.3.1.41.
With the formula, "The breath belongs to Indra," he touches the portion of the animal that has been cut off, [reciting]: "May it settle in every limb... may they rejoice. 5.3.1.42.
With the formula, "Thou art glory," he proceeds with the fat-offering (*vasāhoma*) using the rib, [reciting]: "May Agni cause thee to ascend... and so forth.

5.3.1.43. With the words, “He stirs away hatred,” he stirs three times; he meditates upon him whom the sacrificer hates. 5.3.1.44. He places them for the Pratiprasthātṛ. 5.3.1.45. He recites the Pañcahotṛ formula over the two offering-spoons. || 7 || [8?]
He recites the *pañcahotṛ* formula over the two *sruva*-ladles. They carry them back. Having placed a splinter of wood for the wife, the Adhvaryus set them down.
5.3.2.2. He says, "Recite the invitatory verse for the oblation of the goat for Indra and Agni."
5.3.2.3. Rising up, the Pratiprasthātṛ takes the *vasāhoma* from the Adhvaryu.
5.3.2.4. He says, "Call for the *āśrāvaṇa*," and [the Adhvaryu] gives the command: "Prompt [the Hotṛ] for the oblation of the goat set forth for Indra and Agni.
5.3.2.5. At the half-verse, "O drinkers of ghee, drink the ghee," the Pratiprasthātṛ offers the *vasāhoma*.
5.3.2.6. "O drinkers of fat, drink the fat...
(8) 5.3.2.7. At the utterance of *vaṣaṭ*, the Adhvaryu offers the oblation.
5.3.2.8. Saying, "Recite for Vanaspati," he takes a portion of the speckled butter with the dipping-spoon (*sruva*).

5.3.2.9. Having poured [the portion] into the *juhū* ladle, he gives the call for the wood-deity (*vānaspati*). At the utterance of *vaṣaṭ*, he makes the offering. 5.3.2.10. While bringing together the *sviṣṭakṛt* portion of the oblation, he says: "Recite the invitatory verse for Agni Sviṣṭakṛt. 5.3.2.11. He says: "Call for the announcement!"—"For Agni Sviṣṭakṛt... [he continues].

5.3.2.12. He offers oblations to the quarters with the formula: “To the quarter, svāhā! To the intermediate quarter, svāhā! To the directed quarter, svāhā! To the separated quarter, svāhā! To the upward quarter, svāhā! May the quarters swell with ghee, svāhā! Homage to the quarters, homage to the quarters! 5.3.2.13. Following the quarters, he offers the oblation of the Pañcahotṛ. 5.3.2.14. Having spoken over the two offering-ladles (*sruc*), having stepped across, having placed the ladle in its proper place, and having sprinkled it with clarified butter, he turns back toward the west; then they set down the *iḍā* for the Hotṛ... [in the interval between the lamps]... which the Brahman pushes toward his chest. [cf. 6.8.2.5]

5.3.2.15. They consume [the portions]. He performs the ritual purification (mārjana). 5.3.2.16. He issues the command: "O Āgnīdh, bring the embers for the supplementary offerings (aupayaja)! and "O Upayaṣṭṛ, sit down; O Brahman, we shall proceed; having placed the fuel-stick, O Āgnīdh, cleanse the fire once each time. 5.3.2.17.
Having brought the embers for the supplementary offerings from the Āhavanīya fire, the Āgnīdh pours them out to the east of the Hotṛ, after spreading two blades of sacrificial grass (barhis).
5.3.2.18. The *upayaṣṭṛ* (the butter-pourer) sits down with the *guda* (intestine).
5.3.2.19. He performs the *anūyāja* offerings with the *pṛṣadājya* (speckled butter).
5.3.2.20. He makes the *upabhṛt* itself serve as the *upabhṛt*; this [same vessel] which contains the *pṛṣadājya* serves as the *juhū*.

5.3.2.21. He says, "Make the announcement! (āśrāvaya). 5.3.2.22. Having given the command, "Prompt for the gods! (devebhyaḥ preṣya), he issues the direction. 5.3.2.23. He performs eleven after-offerings (anūyāja).

5.3.2.24. When it is said, "O Maitrāvaruṇa, recite the offering prayer," then the Upayaṣṭṛ makes the secondary offerings (*upayaj*), cutting off a portion of the rectum (*guda*) without piercing through it and without turning it over, with the formula: "Go to the ocean, svāhā! (1.3.11a1). 5.3.2.25. With the formula: "Go to Agni Vaiśvānara, svāhā! (1.3.11, last), he finally offers the entire rectum, ending with: "For the waters thee, for the plants! (1.3.11b). 5.3.2.26. He wipes his hands on the sacrificial grass (*barhis*) while reciting: "Bestow mind upon my heart" (1.3.11c).

5.3.2.27. The *upayaṣṭṛ* makes the sacrificer recite: "May I obtain a body, skin, son, and grandson" (TS 1.3.11d). 5.3.2.28. Having performed the after-offerings (*anūyāja*) and having stepped around, he anoints the *svaru* with the formula: "The controller for the sake of control. 5.3.2.29.
With the formula, "Here is stability," he places it in the offering-ladle; [he continues]: "Here is support, here is self-support."

5.3.2.30. He offers this oblation with the formula: “May your smoke go to heaven; may your flame fill the intermediate space; may you fill the earth with ashes, svāhā! 5.3.2.31. At this point, if they intend to throw the sacrificial post (yūpa) into the fire, he throws it after the offering.
5.3.2.32. Having returned, he separates the two ladles (srucau) with the two Vājavatī verses.

5.3.2.33. With the *śaṃyu*-formula, he scatters the *prastara* grass-bundle and the enclosing sticks (*paridhi*) together. 5.3.2.34. Having gone outside, they perform the *saṃyāja* offerings for the wives of the gods. He offers butter to Soma, butter to Tvaṣṭṛ, and butter to Rākā. 5.3.2.35. While spreading [the butter] and cutting the portions, he says: "Recite the invitatory verse for the wives of the gods."
5.3.2.36. He cuts portions from both the back and the front of the outstretched *viṣkalī*. 5.3.2.37. He pours clarified butter over them and anoints them back.
5.3.2.38. He says, "Call for the *āśrāvaṇa*," and [the *āgnīdhra* responds], "Sacrifice to the wives of the gods. At the utterance of *vaṣaṭ*, he makes the offering.
5.3.2.39. "Recite for Agni Gṛhapati," he says, while spreading [the base of clarified butter] and cutting [the portion].
5.3.2.40. From the northern half of the lower rib, he cuts a thick piece of flesh from the edge.
5.3.2.41. He pours clarified butter over it twice. He does not smear [the blade] back.

5.3.2.42. He says, "Āśrāvaya," and then, "Sacrifice to Agni Gṛhapati. 5.3.2.43. When the *vaṣaṭ* has been uttered, he makes the offering on the northern half, passing over the previous offerings. 5.3.2.44. Having placed the *iḍā* upon the palm turned upwards, and having performed this for the *agnīdh* with the *śaṃyu-formula*, and having offered the *phalīkaraṇa-homa* of clarified butter, he goes forward to the east and offers three *samiṣṭayajus* oblations with [the formula]: "Go to the sacrifice... in the wind" (1.4.44g, omitting the first word).
5.3.2.45. With the verse, “This is your seasonal womb,” he causes the fire to ascend into the two kindling woods (araṇis).

With the verse, “This is your seasonal womb,” he causes the fire to ascend into the two kindling woods; with the verse, “That which is yours... wealth,” if he performs the *udavasāna* (final departure).

5.3.3.2. Or, if he is unable [to do so], having first consigned the fire into a wooden splinter (*śakala*) with the formula, “I am thou,” he releases it into the other *āhavanīya* fire with the formula, “Thou art me, O Jātavedas. 5.3.3.3. With the formula, “Whatever debt remains unpaid by me” (TS 3.3.8b), he approaches the northern corner of the altar with the words, “by which... I become [free from debt]. 5.3.3.4. With the formula, “O consumer of all, I offer thee into the mouth of the consumer of all, svāhā! (TS 3.3.8c1 + svāhā), the sacrificer and his wife offer parched barley flour (*saktu*) into the forest fire with their joined palms.

5.3.3.5. With the words, "from that which has been eaten, one [is born]" (TS 3.3.8c2–4d), he strikes his hands together; and with the words, "from that which has not been offered, one [is born] from the gathering... 3.3.8c,d ... [he becomes] non-existent. 5.3.3.6. Or [he recites]: "O you, lord of the cloud, grant us water" (TS 3.3.8e); or "...grant us vigor... (l.c. e); or with the verse beginning "O God, bestower of abundance" (TS 3.3.8f), [he addresses] the Āditya [with the words] "...thousandfold... prosperity" (g-f); and with the verse beginning "Seeking heroic strength" (TS 3.5.5h), [he addresses] the form [or the sacrificial post] with the words "...of wealth... stand firm" (TS 3.5.5h).
5.3.3.7. If [the fire] stands still, this...
5.3.3.8. If [the fire] has been cast down, they take up the wooden sword (sphya) and a vessel of water, and go out with the heart-spit.

5.3.3.9. Having gone between the pit (cātvāla) and the rubbish-heap (utkara), having dug up the ground to the east of the sacrificial post (yūpa) outside the altar with the wooden sword, [he says]: "O food, protect the earth!"
5.3.3.10. He sprinkles water [from the vessel] with the words, “Break the leather bag! 5.3.3.11.

With the words, “Thou art pain” (ŚB 1.3.11e), he casts away the heart-spike, its point turned away from himself, at the junction of the dry and the moist, with the words, “That [pain] we cast upon him whom we hate” (ŚB 1.3.11e).

5.3.3.12. He worships [the waters] with the words, “From every station, O King” (ŚB 1.3.11f + ?), [saying]: “From here, O King Varuṇa, release us; in the waters is the golden house of King Varuṇa, which has been prepared. Thence the King, whose vow is firm, beholds all laws.”

5.3.3.13. Having sprinkled water around [the fire] with the mantra, "May the waters and plants be friendly to us," they return without looking back, saying, "[The waters and plants] are unfriendly... we hate them. 5.3.3.14.
Having moved away from the sacrificial ground, he offers these oblations, provided that he moves away. 5.3.3.15.

If, however, he does not move away, he offers the *daśahotṛ* formula with four spoonfuls of clarified butter into the *gārhapatya* fire; the *ṣaḍḍhotṛ* into the *anvāhāryapacana*; the *pañcahotṛ* into the *āmātya*; and the *caturhotṛ* into the *sabhyā*.
5.3.3.16. Having arrived, he spreads the clarified butter twice. He pours the curd [into it]. He sprinkles [the butter] over it twice. 5.3.3.17.

He offers that [oblation] in the Āhavanīya fire with the formula: "The crawling, moving [substance], rich in ghee, belonging to Iḍā" (TA 3.11.12); and [he adds]: "The gods found [it]; may it be a source of delight, svāhā! 5.3.3.18.
With the formula, "Return with strength," he offers the curd in the Gārhapatya fire with [the words]: "Again from all sides, svāhā!"
5.3.3.19. With the mantra, "Return with wealth, svāhā" (1.5.3k + svāhā), and [with] "O Agni, overflow... svāhā" (1.5.3k ... pari svāhā). 5.3.3.20.
From this point on, he offers only the full-offering (pūrṇāhuti).
5.3.3.22. Having enclosed [the fire], he takes four spoonfuls for the Āhavanīya fire.
5.3.3.23. Having filled [the vessel], he recites the *saptahotṛ* formula, beginning with "Sevenfold art thou. 5.3.3.24. He places this *ṛc* in the middle.
5.3.3.25. Having placed a fuel-stick on the fire, he offers an oblation for the *hotṛ*; he gives it to another.
The animal sacrifice (paśubandha) is concluded. The animal sacrifice is concluded.
Thus ends the third section (anuvāka).
Thus ends the fifth chapter.
